{{Use Irish English|date=May 2019}}
'''Henry Hickman Harte''' (1790–1848) was an Irish [[mathematician]] and [[clergyman]].

==Life==
Harte, the son of a solicitor, was born in the county of [[Limerick, Ireland]] in 1790. 

He entered [[Trinity College Dublin]] in 1806, and became a Scholar in 1809. He earned his BA in 1811 (and MA in 1823).<ref>{{cite web |url= https://cardcolm.org/AIMM.html |title= Annals of Irish Mathematics and Mathematicians |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Colm Card |publisher= |access-date= 10 June 2026 |quote=}}</ref> He served as the [[Donegall Lecturer in Mathematics]] from 1827 to 1832.<ref>[http://digitalcollections.tcd.ie/home/index.php?DRIS_ID=LCN10378529_0003 Alumni Dublinenses] 1935 edition, p. 376</ref> 

In 1831 Harte accepted the college living of [[Cappagh, County Tyrone|Cappagh]], diocese of Derry, co. Tyrone. He died on Sunday, 5 April 1848, having preached on the same day in his church, where he was also buried. 

==Publications==

Harte translated [[Pierre-Simon Laplace|Laplace]]'s ''Système du Monde''.<ref>{{cite web |url=  https://www.thriftbooks.com/a/henry-hickman-1790-1848-harte/5832825/?msockid=19db67fcac0361053b3271a9ad79605b |title= Henry Hickman, 1790-1848 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= Thrift Books |publisher= |access-date= 10 June 2026 |quote=}}</ref> He also added 'Mathematical Proofs and Explanatory Remarks,' Dublin, 1830.

He published a translation of [[Siméon Denis Poisson|Poisson's]] ''Mécanique, with Notes'', 2 vols. London, 1842, 8vo.<ref>{{cite web |url=   https://catalogue.nli.ie/Record/vtls000189556 |title= Henry Hickman, 1790-1848 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date= |website= National Library of Medicine |publisher= |access-date= 10 June 2026 |quote=}}</ref> 

He commenced another of Laplace's ''Mécanique Céleste''.<ref>{{Cite DNB|wstitle=Harte, Henry Hickman|volume=25}}</ref><gallery>
